questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : The higher acids are wax like solids and are practically odourless due to their low volatility.
Statement-II : Carboxylic acids upto nine carbon atoms are higher boiling point liquids than carbonyl compounds and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and II are correct.
Both statement I and II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement-I:
"The higher acids are wax like solids and are practically odourless due to their low volatility."
- True
- Reason: Higher carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{C}>10\)) have large molar mass and strong van der Waals forces \(\rightarrow\) low volatility \(\rightarrow\) wax-like solids \(\rightarrow\) almost odourless.
Statement-II:
"Carboxylic acids up to nine carbon atoms are higher boiling point liquids than carbonyl compounds and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses."
- True
- Reason: Carboxylic acids form dimers via strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which greatly increases boiling points (even more than alcohols, aldehydes, and ketones of similar size).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : The reaction of alcohol with carboxylic acid is carried out in presence of small amount of concentrated sulphuric acid. This reaction is reversible and therefore, water is removed as soon as it formed.
Statement-II : Reaction of alcohol with acid chloride is carried in presence of base (pyridine) which do not neutralize HCl which is formed during the reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statements I and statements II are correct.
questions.solution:
Statement-I:
"The reaction of alcohol with carboxylic acid is carried out in presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4\). This reaction is reversible and water is removed as soon as it is formed."
- This is Fischer esterification:
\(\mathrm{RCOOH}+\mathrm{R}^{\prime} \mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4} \mathrm{RCOOR} \mathrm{R}^{\prime}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\)
- The reaction is reversible, and to drive it forward, water is removed.
Statement-I is correct.
Statement-II:
"Reaction of alcohol with acid chloride is carried in presence of base (pyridine) which do not neutralize HCl formed during the reaction."
- Reaction:
\(\mathrm{RCOCl}+\mathrm{R}^{\prime} \mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\text { pyridine }} \mathrm{RCOOR}^{\prime}+\mathrm{HCl}\)
- Here pyridine's role is to neutralize the HCl formed (otherwise HCl would protonate alcohol and stop the reaction).
- The statement says pyridine "does not neutralize HCl," which is wrong.
Statement-II is incorrect.

questions.q:
Assertion: Benzoic acid does not undergo Freidel Crafts reaction.
Reason: The carboxyl group in benzoic acid donates electrons into the ring through resonance.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct statements, and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
Both assertion and reason are correct statements, but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
Assertion is correct, but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong, but reason is correct statement.
questions.solution:
Why:
- Benzoic acid doesn't undergo Friedel-Crafts (alkylation/acylation) because the -COOH group is strongly deactivating: it withdraws electrons by -M (resonance) and -I (inductive) effects and also complexes with \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\), killing the ring's reactivity.
- The reason given is false:-COOH does not donate electrons into the ring; it withdraws them.

questions.solution:
- Assertion: Carboxylic acids have greater boiling point than alcohols \(\rightarrow\) True.
Carboxylic acids show stronger intermolecular forces than alcohols.
- Reason: Carboxylic acids can form dimers in solution \(\rightarrow\) True.
They form cyclic dimers via two hydrogen bonds between two - COOH groups. This dimerization effectively doubles molecular mass and strengthens intermolecular attraction.
- Since the reason correctly explains the assertion, the correct answer is:
(a) Both assertion and reason are correct statements, and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.q:
Assertion: Chloro acetic acid has higher pKa value than Acetic acid.
Reason: The - I effect of Cl further stabilises the carboxylate anion formed by the loss of the proton.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct statements, and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
Both assertion and reason are correct statements, but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
Assertion is correct, but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong, but reason is correct statement.
questions.solution:
- Fact check:
- Acetic acid: pKa \(\approx 4.76\)
- Chloroacetic acid: pKa \(\approx 2.86\) (much lower, hence stronger acid).
- Assertion: Chloroacetic acid has higher pKa than acetic acid \(\rightarrow\) False (it has lower pKa).
- Reason: The -1 effect of Cl stabilises the carboxylate anion formed after deprotonation \(\rightarrow\) True. Because chlorine is electronegative, it pulls electron density away, dispersing the negative charge on the carboxylate ion, thus stabilising it. This increases acidity (lowers pKa).

questions.q:
Which of the following reactions yield carboxylic acids.
(A) \(\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}\)
(B) \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \longrightarrow\)
(C) \(\mathrm{PhCN}+\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{\oplus} \longrightarrow\)
(D) \(\mathrm{PhOH}+\mathrm{CHCl}_3+\mathrm{KOH} \longrightarrow\)
options: A, B and C are correct
questions.solution:
(A) \(\mathrm{RMgX}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \rightarrow\) (on hydrolysis) \(\rightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{COOH}\)
Yes, this is a standard reaction of Grignard reagent with \(\mathrm{CO}_2\), giving carboxylic acid.
(B) \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \rightarrow\) Salicylic acid (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction)
Yes, this is the Kolbe reaction, which yields ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).
(C) \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{N}+\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{COOH}\)
Hydrolysis of nitriles in acidic medium gives carboxylic acids.
(D) \(\mathrm{PhOH}+\mathrm{CHCl}_3+\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow\) Salicylaldehyde (Reimer-Tiemann reaction)
This gives salicylaldehyde (-CHO group), not a carboxylic acid.

questions.solution:
The acidity of carboxylic acid is directly proportional to the acid dissociation constant. But it is inversely proportional to the pKa value because the pKa is equal to the -logKa. So, the order of acidity of given acids depends upon the -M,-I effect. It is directly proportional to the -M,-I effect. 

The acetic acid is least acidic. So, it has the pKa value of 4.76. After that acidity of benzoic acid. So, it has the pKa value of 4.19. After that acidity of p-nitrobenzoic acid. So, it has the pKa value of 3.41. The compound F3CCOOH is most acidic. So, it has the pKa value of 0.23.
